== Biography ==

The Queen—by title, the Queen of Hearts—is the supreme authority of the realm, ruling from her throne with an iron hand and the constant threat of execution.

Her most characteristic response to any displeasure or misdeed is swift judgment and capital punishment. When the Hatter begins to sing at a gathering, she jumps up and cries out, "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!" When the royal game of croquet descends into chaos—players quarreling without waiting for turns and fighting over the hedgehogs—the Queen becomes "in a furious passion," stamping about the field and shouting "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" approximately once every minute. Those of Wonderland regard her as "dreadfully savage," and the inhabitants are known to be "dreadfully fond of beheading people," a practice that owes much to the Queen's judicial temperament.

She commands through fear and absolute authority. When unknown visitors arrive, she demands with severity: "Who is this?" and issues swift dismissals to those who displease her—she calls the Knave of Hearts an "Idiot!" with cutting contempt when he fails to meet her expectations. She sits in formal judgment at the official proceedings of the realm, her word law and her justice swift.

Even in memory and dream, the Queen's presence looms large. Those who have left her realm retain the echo of her "shrill voice, ordering off her unfortunate guests to execution"—a haunting reminder that her authority defines the emotional landscape of Wonderland itself.

== Narrative role ==

The Queen of Hearts rules Wonderland with capricious authority and a taste for swift executions. She first surfaces through an invitation to a croquet game, though her reputation precedes her: the Hatter had already quarreled with Time itself after she accused him of murdering the time, her response being an immediate order for his head. When Alice encounters the Queen's magnificent procession and deliberately refuses to bow, the Queen nearly executes her for the insolence—only the King's intervention, noting that Alice is merely a child, restrains her judgment.

The croquet game itself becomes a spectacle of chaos and terror under the Queen's direction. She plays in a furious passion, stamping about and shouting "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" with relentless frequency, sometimes once a minute. The game itself—played with flamingos as mallets and hedgehogs as balls, with card-soldiers serving as wickets—dissolves into constant quarreling and absent rules. Yet in this pandemonium, Alice saves three gardeners from execution by concealing them in a flower pot, outwitting the Queen's soldiers. As the game continues, the Queen sentences numerous players to execution with scarcely a hesitation, her pronouncements falling without end.

The Gryphon later reveals a peculiar truth to Alice: the Queen's death sentences are empty—no one actually dies despite the constant proclamations. The Queen appears again with sudden violence, threatening the Duchess with execution and sending her fleeing. At last, the Queen presides over the trial of the Knave of Hearts, accused of stealing her tarts, her authority and peculiar brutality dominating the proceedings.

== Personality ==

The Queen is volatile and violent by temperament. She erupts into fury at the slightest provocation—when the Hatter sings poorly, she shouts "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!" with immediate, unthinking rage. Beheading is her answer to any offense, however minor or absurd. During the croquet game, as players quarrel and chaos reigns, she stamps about "in a furious passion," shouting threats of execution "about once in a minute." Those around her live in constant dread, knowing that to displease her is to risk death.

She is imperious and will not tolerate disobedience or even hesitation. She dismisses the Knave as an "Idiot!" and speaks to Alice with cutting severity. Her impatience manifests in small, sharp gestures—she tosses her head "impatiently"—and dominates her larger actions: she cannot suffer disruption, inefficiency, or anything that thwarts her will. In her presence, obedience is the only survival strategy.

The chaos of her realm—the croquet game with no rules, the court in constant upheaval, the casual executions—does not suggest a system broken or mismanaged. Rather, it is a direct expression of her nature: a ruler who imposes order through fear and maintains authority by the perpetual threat of death. She is Wonderland's terror made flesh.

== Relationships ==

'''[[King]]''' — They share the throne of Hearts together, and he is one of the few figures who can moderate her impulses, laying his hand upon her arm to plead for mercy toward those she would condemn.

'''[[Alice]]''' — The Queen perceives Alice as an offense and demands her execution when Alice fails to show proper deference, though Alice herself responds with spirited defiance, declaring "Nonsense!" to the Queen's threats.

'''[[Knave]]''' — The Queen commands the Knave directly, addressing him with contempt and calling him "Idiot," expecting his immediate and careful obedience.

'''[[Duchess]]''' — The Queen invites the Duchess to participate in her croquet games, suggesting a social connection between them, however fraught it may be.

'''[[Hatter]]''' — The Hatter's singing draws the Queen's swift and violent displeasure; she condemns him to execution for what she perceives as an offense to propriety.

== Trivia ==

* During games and social gatherings, the Queen demonstrates poor sportsmanship, quarreling constantly with other players and fighting over the pieces at hand.
* She appears unconcerned with fixed rules or fair play, expecting events to conform to her will regardless of precedent.
* The executions she orders have become so commonplace that it is considered a wonder that anyone remains alive in her realm.
